title: DHCP Systems: Address Management
subject: Network Infrastructure
description: Manage IP allocation, solve scope exhaustion, and configure relay agents in a routed environment.
reportOverview: This module validates your ability to manage the IPv4 lifecycle and troubleshoot delivery failures across VLAN boundaries.

tickets.title: Intermittent Connectivity in the Cafe
tickets.summary: Users in the guest cafe are getting 169.254.x.x addresses. Some users can connect, but new arrivals cannot.
artifact: Scope Statistics: 253 of 254 addresses in use
Red Herring: DHCP Service Status is 'Running'

triage.q: What does a 169.254.x.x address indicate about the client's attempt to get an IP?
options: The client has a static IP conflict
The client failed to receive a DHCP Offer/Ack (APIPA)
The DHCP server is assigning 'Emergency' IPs
The wireless access point is encrypted

diagnosis.q: The scope is 100% full. Why are addresses not being freed up when users leave the cafe?
options: The lease duration is too long (8 days), keeping IPs reserved for inactive clients
The DHCP database is full and cannot delete records
The router is blocking the DHCP Release packets
The users are not logging out of the captive portal

fix.q: What is the best configuration change to ensure high-turnover areas like a cafe always have available IPs?
options: Shorten the Lease Duration to 2 or 4 hours
Expand the subnet to a /16 immediately
Disable the DHCP scope and restart it daily
Tell users to release their IP manually

debrief.summary: Scope exhaustion is common in 'transient' environments.
debrief.takeaway: Matching lease duration to user behavior (short stay = short lease) prevents 'ghost' reservations from blocking new users.

tickets.title: New VLAN 20 Cannot Reach DHCP
tickets.summary: A new department has been moved to VLAN 20. They are physically connected but cannot get an IP from the central DHCP server on VLAN 10.
artifact: Router: Routing is enabled between VLAN 10 and 20
Red Herring: Firewall logs show no blocked traffic

triage.q: Why do DHCP Discover packets fail to reach a server on a different VLAN by default?
options: DHCP uses broadcasts, which do not cross router boundaries
The server doesn't know the route back to the client
VLAN 20 is inherently less secure than VLAN 10
The DHCP server is restricted to a single NIC

diagnosis.q: What component is missing on the VLAN 20 gateway to allow it to 'forward' these requests?
options: A static route to the DHCP server
A DHCP Relay Agent or 'IP Helper-Address'
An Access Control List (ACL)
A DNS Forwarder

fix.q: How should you configure the Router/Switch to fix the delivery issue?
options: Add 'ip helper-address 10.0.10.5' to the VLAN 20 interface
Move the DHCP server into VLAN 20
Enable 'Promiscuous Mode' on the client NICs
Create a Superscope on the DHCP Server

debrief.summary: DHCP Relay (IP Helper) is the bridge between broadcast and unicast.
debrief.takeaway: The relay agent catches the local broadcast and sends it directly to the server, allowing centralized DHCP for the whole enterprise.
